trim.title: Trim video
trim.subtitle: Choose a segment, preview it and export an MP4 video
trim.heroNote:
Keep the best moments
Share them easily!

steps.1: Choose or drop a local video
steps.3: Choose the end of your segment

tips.1: Short videos are faster to process
tips.2: Drag the sliders or enter seconds
tips.3: MP4 output, up to 1080 px on the long edge
tips.4: Videos are not uploaded to a server

1.q: Is there a file size limit?
1.a: Yes. Up to 100 MB, ten minutes and 4K resolution. Short clips under 30 MB work best on phones.

2.a: The segment is re-encoded at frame level as MP4 H.264/AAC, up to 1080 px on the long edge. Quality and metadata may differ from the original.

3.q: Why is the first run slower?
3.a: The first run downloads a processing engine of about 32 MB. Processing speed depends on the video and your device.

trim.emptyHint: Upload a video to choose the segment to keep.
trim.privacy: Your video is processed on your device.
trim.resultHint: The processed video will appear here for preview and download.

read.title: Read text aloud
read.subtitle: Paste text or upload a document, choose a voice and listen
read.heroNote:
Less reading effort
Listen to what matters!

steps.1: Paste text or choose a document
steps.2: Review the text to be read
steps.3: Choose a voice and reading speed
steps.5: Pause, resume or export WAV with Vietnamese voice

tips.1: Use Vietnamese voice if your device lacks one
tips.2: Slow down the voice when needed
tips.3: Increase the reading view font size
tips.4: File content is retained when switching input modes

1.a: Vietnamese voice supports WAV export. Device voice uses the voices available on your device and does not export audio files.

2.a: Vietnamese voice downloads data on first use, then processes on your device. Device voices may use online services. When enabled, extracting content from a link requires internet.

3.a: Yes. Open File to see supported formats and review the extracted text. Long documents are divided into selectable parts.

read.previewHint: Text in the selected part. Press Read text to begin.
read.emptyHint: Add content in step 1, choose a voice and start listening.
read.wavHint: Vietnamese voice can export WAV for the selected part.
read.deviceHint: Device voice plays directly on your device. Choose Vietnamese voice for WAV export.

compress.title: Compress video
compress.subtitle: Reduce video size and export MP4 in your browser
compress.emptyHint: Choose a video from your device to preview and adjust the output.
compress.resultHint: Check the file size, preview and download the compressed video.

steps.1: Upload a video from your device.
steps.2: Choose light, balanced or strong compression.
steps.3: Choose a maximum edge of 720 or 1080 px.
steps.4: Start compression and wait for it to finish.

tips.1: Keep the original video to compare quality.
tips.3: An already optimized video may not get smaller.
tips.4: Video processing runs on your device without uploading the file.

1.a: Up to 100 MB, 10 minutes and 3840 × 2160 pixels. Processing also depends on device memory.

2.a: Output is MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio when the source contains audio.

3.q: Is the video uploaded to a server?
3.a: No. The processing engine loads when needed and runs in your browser. Keep the page open during processing.

gif.title: Video to GIF
gif.subtitle: Turn a short clip into a looping animation on your device
gif.emptyHint: Choose a video from your device to preview and adjust the output.
gif.resultHint: Preview the animation and download the GIF after processing.

steps.1: Upload a video from your device.
steps.2: Choose a clip up to 20 seconds long.
steps.4: Preview your clip, then create the GIF.

tips.3: Lower width and frame rate help reduce size.
tips.4: Video processing runs on your device without uploading the file.

1.a: Up to 100 MB, 10 minutes and 3840 × 2160 pixels. Processing also depends on device memory.

2.q: Why is the GIF file large?
2.a: GIF works best for short clips. Reduce duration, width or frame rate to reduce size.

3.q: Is the video uploaded to a server?
3.a: No. The processing engine loads when needed and runs in your browser. Keep the page open during processing.
